title: USRP X440 Tool
tagline: A tool that turns signal capture on the USRP X440 — a direct-sampling SDR — into a few simple inputs.
summary: A web interface and Python backend that make Ettus' direct-sampling USRP X440 SDR easy for researchers to use.
overview: The USRP X440 is a software-defined radio (SDR) built on a direct-sampling architecture: it digitises signals straight at their radio frequency, with no intermediate-frequency stage. That makes it powerful — but also tricky to set up for every capture.
The goal was to simplify the whole capture pipeline: researchers describe the signal they want to record, and the tool works out everything the device needs.
The solution is a web interface with a Python backend that handles all the pre-capture calculations and [finish this sentence — e.g. configures the device and runs the capture].
It was also my bachelor's thesis for the Computer Engineering degree at UAB: a tracking station for LEO satellite mega-constellations built on a programmable high-speed RFSoC device.
